20210101.text: So what did you guys do in the Raiden Shogun's Plane of Euthymia anyway?

20210102.text: Is the Vision Hunt Decree abolished?

20210105.text: Oh, gotcha... Paimon was super worried, y'know.

20210106.text: So maybe the reason Yae Miko is looking for us now is 'cause she wants to thank us? Let's go find her.

20210243.text: What would you like to know about?

20210302.text: That puppet was built with technology that has been lost to time. Perhaps she, as a god, is the only one privy to the knowledge of its origins...

20210303.text: Still... there is one other thing on this topic that I suspect you may be curious to know.

20210304.text: Before Ei began modifying her own godly form, she took it upon herself to create a prototype puppet...

20210305.text: So... you mean there are three Raiden Shoguns!?

20210306.text: No, the prototype was merely a proof of concept. Its appearance and intellect were not based on Ei. It was a test.

20210307.text: The original plan was for Ei to simply discard it. But perhaps Ei thought this to be too cruel, because in the end she chose only to seal the power within it.

20210308.text: Later, this puppet wandered Inazuma as an ordinary human male with his own consciousness, until... the Fatui took an interest in him.

20210310.text: Some eccentric geniuses in the ranks of the Fatui made adjustments to the prototype, not only unsealing his power, but very likely rendering him even more formidable than his original specifications.

20210312.text: Mm-hmm. The object of divine creation is the one who has now taken possession of the Gnosis... and the prototype puppet is now known as "The Balladeer."

20210313.text: What in the... What a crazy story!

20210314.text: It is, isn't it? Who can say whether it's coincidence or destiny.

20210201.text: Why hello... if it isn't the triumphant Traveler. And why might you be visiting the Shrine? A sign of piety, perhaps?

20210202.text: You literally told us to come meet you here!

20210203.text: Haha... I was just joking. I've been waiting for you.

20210204.text: Seems like someone's in a pretty good mood.

20210205.text: Mm-hmm. Catching up with an old friend I hadn't seen in years was truly delightful.

20210206.text: By the way... I heard that you had a duel before the throne, with a Fatui Harbinger no less. Courageous and astute — I must say, I am most impressed.

20210209.text: Defeating Signora head-on in a duel means that your strength exceeds my expectations.

20210210.text: Still, you did end up victorious. I gather congratulations are in order.

20210211.text: Ah, it sure feels good to finally thwart a Fatui plan for once.

20210212.text: They caused plenty of trouble along the way, but at the very least, they didn't get their hands on another Gnosis!

20210213.text: Wait a second... did you say "Gnosis"?

20210214.text: As in, the little thing that looks something like a chess piece?

20210215.text: Yep, that's the one! You've seen one, too? Gnoses belong to The Seven — they're what keep them connected to Celestia!

20210221.text: Well... how else was I supposed to save your skin from The Balladeer, exactly?

401060101.text: Twenty years ago, the Akademiya had just received Sachin's estate. To celebrate the huge investment, the Akademiya Extravaganza that year was grander than usual.

401060102.text: I was very young then, and I remember seeing posters for the Interdarshan Championship all over the city. I couldn't help but mention it to my father. I even told him that I really liked the look of the diadem — it was so unique.

401060103.text: So he said, "Why don't I win it, so I can let you play with it for a few days?"

401060104.text: That made me very happy, and I nodded enthusiastically. But to my surprise, he didn't win, and when he got back home, he seemed extremely depressed.

401060105.text: Later, he left home, saying that he wanted to do some investigating in the desert... The quicksand got him not long after that...

401060106.text: ...For many years, I couldn't face up to it at all. If I'd just kept my mouth shut, maybe none of it would have ever happened.

401060107.text: Your father may have seen Sachin that year.

401060108.text: Wait... So the person we came across in our investigation, who went into the desert twenty years ago... it was...

401060110.text: ...Haha... Is that why Sachin thought I looked familiar? I can't believe it...

401060111.text: ...My father was always too kind for his own good. Sachin's research would have saddened him greatly — he must have gone into the desert when he heard about it to find those who were still suffering... It all makes sense now.

401060113.text: I've tried telling myself so many times over the years that maybe his sudden depression wasn't because he didn't win the competition, maybe something else was going on that I wasn't aware of... But in the end, it all started with me mentioning the competition to him.

401060115.text: Don't worry. I... I destroyed the diadem. There will never be another tragedy like this again. Never again...

401060116.text: (Don't mention the results of the investigation.)

401060117.text: Sorry... My mind was still on the Championship. Look at me, rambling away.

401060118.text: You look really upset... Are you sure you're okay?

401060119.text: I'm fine. What's past is past — we need to look towards the future.

401060201.text: Where were you while the rest of us were eating together?

401060202.text: I don't recall being obligated to report my whereabouts to you.

401060203.text: Did you go find another hidey-hole to read in? You need to change your ways, you know. You can't survive on books alone.

401060204.text: Surviving on meals paid for by you would be harder still.

401060206.text: Hmph, whatever, it doesn't take a genius to guess what you've been up to... You were investigating Sachin, weren't you? It was obvious from your notes. However, I don't believe his research alone would've been enough to pique your interest.

401060207.text: His way of doing things is disturbing, while you... Well, to be fair, your philosophy disgusts me too, but you and Sachin are nothing alike. I don't imagine your views intersect at all. Egoism and nihilism are not the same thing.

401060208.text: My personal interest aside, Sachin's legacy is not entirely meaningless — he conducted experiments on a great scale, and left his findings behind.

401060209.text: Also, thanks for the compliment. But I'm actually just passing through — I didn't come here for the conversation. Well, not this one at least.

401060210.text: What do you mean? What topic of conversation could be more sacred among scholars than the exploration of differing philosophies?

401060211.text: Well, based on what I've learned, Sachin and his "disturbing way of doing things" — as you put it — is very likely to have met your father twenty years ago.

401060213.text: ...Wait, so... No, surely that doesn't mean...

401060214.text: Hah. So that's why he thought I looked familiar. My father must've gone into the desert due to his influence...

401060217.text: Good thing I shattered that diadem. From now on... nothing like that will ever have to happen again.

401060218.text: The boundaries of knowledge are ever-expanding. Someone else will inevitably pick up the same line of research one day, and Vahumana regards it as a reasonable research direction.

401060219.text: Oh, not this again... Even if you're right, and people are bound to fall into the same intellectual traps, things won't necessarily go the same way again next time.

401060220.text: You have to admit that the actions of one individual don't always predict the behavior of the group, and vice-versa. Take Sachin, for instance. He's quite an anomaly.

401060221.text: And so is the one who stopped him — you. Conflicts of this nature are indeed exceptional, but it will occur again in the future.

401060222.text: You said it yourself — the actions of one individual cannot predict the behavior of a whole group. You know that not everyone would have chosen as you did.

401060224.text: ...Even so, I stand by my views. You can forget about trying to convince me.

401060225.text: That's fine. We've been arguing over this for years, and I don't hold any hope of you understanding. The issue we're debating has long since moved on from who's right and who's wrong.

401060226.text: ...Thanks for letting me know all this.

401060228.text: I said, thanks for letting me know. Hey! Stop acting like you didn't hear me! You're doing this on purpose, aren't you!?

401060229.text: They say that earnest thanks should be given thrice, so... One more time, please.

401060301.text: Well, how did it go? I assume that Lord Sangemah Bay's assistance helped you discover something, yes?

401060303.text: Sachin was not a good person, and there's definitely something wrong with that Diadem of Knowledge!

401060306.text: Then in that case, shouldn't you be doing something about it?

401060307.text: For instance, telling the Akademiya that they should give up the Diadem—

401060308.text: We already told the Akademiya, but...

401060312.text: Calm down, Dori! Why are you getting so worked up?

401060315.text: Ah, this was supposed to be the perfect plan! I feed you the information, you discover the issue with the diadem, and then I just wait until the Akademiya sells it off at a low price...

401060316.text: And now it was all for nothing! Grr, curse that Kaveh! The interest rate on the Mora he owes me is about to get much higher!

401060317.text: Ohhh, so that's why you told us about this. Yeah, Paimon did think you were being unusually generous...

401060318.text: My diadem! Ugh, I'm furious! That's it, no extension on his payment this month, no matter what reason he gives!

401060501.text: Hello, I am the Vizier. Do you need any help?

401060502.text: If you wished to see the Interdarshan Championship, then unfortunately, the portion taking part in Sumeru City has concluded.

401060503.text: ...Hold on, on closer inspection you seem to be that guest commentator.

401060504.text: My apologies. I thank you for the contributions you made to the Akademiya Extravaganza. It's all thanks to your help that the first round concluded so smoothly.

401060505.text: But I might have been overindulgent in my praise. I heard the Interdarshan Championship has also encountered similar difficulties before... This time, both the contestants and viewers have been spared any harm. How fortunate.

401060601.text: Greetings. You may call me "Master Treasure Appraiser, Prospective Antiques Collector, and Future Prominent Businessman Feresht."

401060602.text: Have you heard? The Akademiya is hosting some kind of celebration along with a competition. Supposedly, the champion's prize is an extremely rare treasure.

401060603.text: I think it was called... the diadem of... something. Ah. It doesn't matter. The first trick to being an expert appraiser of treasures is to avoid getting intimidated by a treasure's name!

401060604.text: In terms of appraising antique collections, I'm only slightly less refined than my father. If you want to know how much a certain treasure is worth, just bring it to me and I'll let you know after a glance.

401060701.text: It's not often that the Akademiya hosts an event like this. We need to increase the number of patrols inside the city for this special occasion.

401060702.text: This isn't even especially for the competition. In fact, it is the increase in tourists that require us to take additional care.

401060703.text: There are no shortage of devious people who are willing to take advantage of these festivities to mask their own nefarious deeds.

401060801.text: ...Should you deny that the Championship rates Darshans based on their scores, please recall that we all entered our respective Darshans via our test scores.

401060802.text: To overlook the scores is to overlook the very basis for all assessments made by the Darshans.

401060803.text: In turn, you should remember before you overemphasize the scores, that they are only representative of how each contestant performs for specific tasks exclusive to the competition.

401060804.text: Moreover, we also need to consider other probabilistic factors such as weather, geography, morale and so on.

401060805.text: Oh? And we didn't need to consider this when we were testing into our Darshans?

401060806.text: A sophistic comparison! My test scores can represent my capabilities, but it does not showcase the totality of what a Darshan represents.

401060807.text: A foolish opinion as usual. No offense intended.

401060808.text: Disagree though you may, scores determine the rankings and results speak for everything.

401060901.text: Even if we find a calm place to think, we will inevitably be interrupted by noisy students.

401060902.text: To be honest, I was never interested in these celebratory events or competitions when I was in the Akademiya.

401060903.text: Winning the Championship doesn't really help add any credit to your research, and any renown gained from it only amounts to some short-lived attention.

401060904.text: ...Realistically speaking, there are few people as practical as I am.

401061002.text: Ah, if I continue my studies down this path, I might just be able to see why there is a separation between my theories and the calculations.

401061003.text: The Interdarshan Championships have done a lot of good this time. If Rtawahist hadn't selected Miss Layla as the representative, I would have never consulted her research.

401061004.text: I can only say that Miss Layla keeps too low a profile. Such incredible research needs to be seen by more people.

401061101.text: A pity that knowledge so great is constrained by matters of Mora...

401061102.text: And when there are wealthy sponsors, the wealth is not fed into valuable research but rather burned on frivolous competitions...

401061103.text: You mean the sponsor? Hm... I haven't heard much about them, but they should be a good person.

401061104.text: Even merchants who think of nothing but profit should not be judged with prejudice so long as they are willing to place emphasis on the development and preservation of knowledge.

401061105.text: ...Because, when it comes down to it, almost anything is better than someone who wastes money.

401061201.text: I didn't expect Tighnari, who rarely shows himself in the city, to participate in the Interdarshan Championship.

401061202.text: I don't know much about Tighnari. He doesn't strike me as someone who is fame-hungry... Perhaps too many people were recommending him, and he didn't want to disappoint them.

401061203.text: Speaking of which, I think he's planning to hold a new lecture next month.

401061204.text: I must note down the time of his lecture before I forget... I can't miss it!

401061301.text: I want a break... Why can't the Akademiya give us some time off during the Extravaganza?

401061302.text: Don't you enjoy watching the competition?

401061303.text: No, I do but... If you think about it, we can only watch the competitions if we have a break, right?

401061304.text: Yeah, that makes sense... Though, watching all my senior classmates represent their Darshans has inadvertently inspired a new drive in me to study!

401061305.text: I've made up my mind. In the future, I'm going to enter the Interdarshan Championship too!

401061306.text: Huh... It's a bit early to be thinking about this, isn't it? Didn't our instructors say that seeking knowledge should be a steady and serious endeavor?

401061307.text: Maybe before considering partaking in a competition that happens once in a blue moon, maybe you should consider which Darshan you want to join first?

401061401.text: It's said that you can see pretty far if you stand high, but the higher you go, the harder it is to see what's right beneath you...

401061402.text: Ah, sorry. I was talking to myself.

401061403.text: If you're looking to join the Akademiya Extravaganza, then you probably got lost to wander this far. You're way past the boundaries of the festivities.

401061501.text: Huh? I didn't think someone would want to chat with me even now. Aren't you joining in on the Akademiya Extravaganza?

401061502.text: Hmm... What fun events are there... Truth be told, I'm not one for such occasions, so I can't say.

401061503.text: However, I don't dislike these celebratory events. The more students join in such galas, the quieter things are over here.

401061602.text: Oh? So you don't exactly know what I do, huh?

401061603.text: No worries. As a matter of fact, that's a good thing. The fewer people who come to talk to me about work, the better — that means our academic environment is a healthy one.

401061604.text: Honestly, I expected a great deal of problems to follow the Akademiya's celebration. I was even ready to head back to the office and prepare for overtime.

401061605.text: But there really haven't been that many people seeking me out. Even the General Mahamatra is on break... Hm. I'm just going to keep resting here.

401061701.text: What a blunder... I won't get to watch the competitions during the day if I'm working nights!

401061702.text: That said... ah, I can't just dip work and go see the competition during the day, haha.

401061703.text: Keeping that in mind gives me some balance. Maybe my classmates might fill me in on what's happening in the competition over some drinks at night.

401061704.text: With the gala comes more tourists, and with more tourists comes an increase to my pay. I might even hear some new drunken jokes! Seems like I'm being well compensated for my time!

401061801.text: Though work is as boring as ever and Zubayr Theater has no new showings, there seems to be no shortage of prospects as of late!

401061802.text: Say, friend, are you going to watch the Interdarshan Championship? I hear Miss Nilou's going to be commentating!

401061803.text: I wasn't much of a student growing up. Felt like I had an allergy to learning. However, after listening to how Miss Nilou breaks things down, the knowledge seems a lot easier for me to grasp.

401061804.text: If you missed Miss Nilou's commentary, it's your loss.

736900201.text: How about it? Care for a game of "Project Connectivity"?

736900203.text: Alright. In that case, if you'll look over this way...

736900205.text: Ah, is that so... It's alright. Our booth will be open for the entire duration of the Gala.

736900206.text: Whenever you feel like having a go, you can just come to me.

736900301.text: I do hope everyone will enjoy the game...

736910201.text: *sigh* Everyone's just too sensitive about academic issues. It's just a toy. Come on...

736910301.text: I wish the older students would stop coming over to ask. This really, truly is just a toy.

736910302.text: Ah? Oh... It's you, Traveler. Would you like to play a round or two of "Gathering of Stars"?

736910304.text: Sure. The astrolabe is over here.

736910306.text: Well, I'll be here at the booth throughout the Gala. If you're of a mind to play, just hit me up.

736920201.text: Was my tone too serious? Ugh, that's not good...

736920202.text: Traveler? Are you here to give "Mimetic Replication" a try?

736920204.text: Alright. In that case, please step over here.

736920206.text: That's fine. My booth will be open throughout the Gala, so you can come over and try the game out any time.

736920301.text: Might this degree of simplification and generalization be too facile, I wonder...

736930201.text: How did this fall to me? Couldn't we have assigned this task to a more experienced senior student?

736940301.text: Hmm. I do hope everyone will be able to experience the joys of archaeology through this activity...

736940401.text: I do hope everyone will be able to experience the joys of archaeology...

736960201.text: Well then, would you like to give "In Truth's Steps" a go?

736960203.text: Good, good. In that case, lend me your ears.

736960205.text: That's alright. I'll be here, and you can come back whenever you'd like to have a go.

736960401.text: No. The mire could not be traversed by human strength.

736960501.text: Yes. Enough to ensure that the Forest Rangers' clothes would not get wet.

736960601.text: Yes. The distance was so great that even shouts could not be heard.

736961001.text: Beydim was <color=#00E1FFFF>not a Forest Ranger</color>, but the Forest Ranger's <color=#00E1FFFF>companion</color>.

736961201.text: This question, I fear, has nothing to do with the story.

736962501.text: Are... these stories still too complex?

736962601.text: Did everyone take a leave permit?

736962605.text: Why was one leave permit slip left in the box?

736962701.text: Hmm... You might want to give these questions a little more thought. You didn't get a single one of them right...

736962801.text: Not bad! I think you're on the right track. One of your answers was correct.

736962901.text: Well done. You got all the answers correct.

736962905.text: The truth of the matter is that the leave permits were indeed put into everyone's hands...

736962909.text: But that final person to take a leave permit took the box that contained them as well.

736962910.text: As such, both the office keys and the letter wound up stuck inside the locked office.

736963001.text: Very good! You've solved two questions, but one remains out of your reach for the moment.

736963206.text: Who was it who last came into contact with the letter?

736963301.text: Hmm... You might want to give these questions a little more thought. You didn't get a single one of them right...

736963401.text: Not bad! I think you're on the right track. One of your answers was correct.

736963501.text: Very good! You've solved two questions, but you still need to solve two more.

736963601.text: Excellent! You truly do have an agile mind. There's only one question left unsolved.

736963701.text: Well done. You got all the answers correct.

736963705.text: Here is the full truth: Bahera took the keys to the office, and when his mentor sent him a letter to ask for them, he sent them in a letter back to the Akademiya.

736963709.text: However, when his letter reached his Darshan, the staff member simply dropped it into Bahera's mentor's office through its letter slot.

736963710.text: As such, both the office keys and the letter wound up stuck inside the locked office.

736963901.text: Not bad! I think you're on the right track. One of your answers was correct.

736964101.text: Well done. You got all the answers correct.

736964105.text: The full truth is this: Beydim was a messenger Dusk Bird used by the Forest Ranger Asti.

736964109.text: After sighting the wild beast, Asti chose to send Beydim out to inform the other Forest Rangers due to the storm impeding travel.

736964110.text: Beydim flew through that storm, and thus got all wet.
